root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: payloadInfo.isNull() == true on this malformed NFLOG TLV stream
root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `pcpp::NflogLayer::parseNextLayer()` trusts the `NFULA_PAYLOAD` lookup, `payloadInfo.isNull()` must remain true for this malformed TLV stream so the function returns at the existing null check instead of constructing an `IPv4Layer` from bytes that cannot hold a full IPv4 header.
root_cause_criterion.description: On the vulnerable original, `getTlvByType(NFULA_PAYLOAD)` returns a non-null record, so `parseNextLayer()` continues into the payload path even though the first 20 bytes of the would-be IPv4 header already extend one byte past the 28-byte backing NFLOG buffer. On the fixed original, the same lookup is null on the same input, so `parseNextLayer()` exits before the sink becomes reachable.

nodes.state: At the vulnerable non-null payload site, the first 20 bytes required for an IPv4 header end at `payload + sizeof(iphdr)`, which is one byte beyond the enclosing NFLOG layer end `m_Data + m_DataLen`.

At the ASan crash site, the destination-address read ends at `dst_field_end_ptr`, which is the same one-past-end address as the vulnerable payload-side IPv4-header boundary and lies beyond the previous NFLOG layer's real backing end.

edges.relation: The same one-past-end IPv4-header boundary computed from `payload + sizeof(iphdr)` in `parseNextLayer()` becomes the destination-field end pointer observed at `getDstIPv4Address()`.
The NFLOG layer's real backing end `m_Data + m_DataLen` is retained as the previous-layer end seen at the later destination-address read sink.
